The master, or the apprentice?|[[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] and [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] discuss the theory|<ref name="Episode 1">{{Film|I}}</ref>}}
The '''Second Sith theory''' was a marginalized theory held by some members of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] during the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]] and later the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. While not officially endorsed by the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]], the theory postulated that the [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] dervish that killed [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] had been a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]]. If this were true, then those who believed that the [[Rule of Two/Legends|Rule of Two]] had been maintained among any [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] who remained hidden suggested there must be a second Sith&mdash;either a [[Sith Master/Legends|master]] or an [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]]. The theory was further advanced by [[Count of Serenno/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku's]] conversation with [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], where he implicated one [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] in manipulating the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]].

==Overview==
===Origin===
{{Quote|He was trained in the Jedi arts. My only conclusion can be that it was&hellip; a Sith Lord.|Qui-Gon Jinn|<ref name="Movie">{{Film|I}}</ref>}}
The theory of the so-called Second [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] originated in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] when the [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] received reports from the [[Theed Royal Palace/Legends|Theed Royal Palace]]. [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] had been [[Battle of Naboo/Legends#Duel in Theed|cut down]] by the same [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] dervish that had [[Duel on Tatooine/Legends|ambushed]] him on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. The Zabrak, [[Sith apparel|garbed]] in [[Color/Legends|black]] and [[Darth Maul's double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|wielding]] a [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|double-bladed lightsaber]] in the style of [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]], was well-versed in the ways of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and drew upon the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] for strength.

While the [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] had seemingly been killed by Jinn's [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], rumors spread when investigations showed that members of [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala's]] [[Naboo Royal Advisory Council/Legends|Advisory Council]] had overheard [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] refer to the Zabrak as "[[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]]."<ref name="SkyeWalkers">''[[SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story]]''</ref> While [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] member [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] privately questioned the idea of a second Sith hiding in the shadows during [[Funeral of Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon's funeral]], neither he nor [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] could determine the truth beyond speculating whether Maul was an apprentice or the master.<ref name="Episode 1" />

===Development===
With the name "Darth Maul" impossible to corroborate there being a second Sith, there seemed to be no other leads.<ref name="SkyeWalkers" /> Despite such fanatics as [[Granta Omega]] cropping up during the turbulent time of the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], the High Council refused to speculate on the matter and counseled patience and [[Meditation/Legends|meditation]] in the matter.

With the lack of evidence providing little relief to those frustrated with the identity of Darth Maul, scant trace accounts of the [[Rule of Two/Legends|Rule of Two]] kept the mystery alive.<ref name="SkyeWalkers" /> Some Jedi suspected that the Sith may have avoided death during the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan]] and gone into [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]]. Others, however, dismissed the notion out-of-hand. Council member [[Ki-Adi-Mundi/Legends|Ki-Adi-Mundi]] was adamant in his belief that the idea was obscene, declaring that the Sith had been extinct for a [[Millennium/Legends|millennium]] and the Order would have detected their return. When accusations arose that [[Count of Serenno/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] was a Sith, Mundi proclaimed him to be a political idealist rather than a Sith.

===Clone Wars===
The theory was revived when Dooku revealed to an imprisoned Kenobi on [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] that a Sith Lord named [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] was secretly in control of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. This control, Dooku alleged, came through Sidious' manipulation of thousands of [[Senator/Legends|Senators]] who unwittingly served the [[Grand Plan/Legends|Sith agenda]].<ref name="SkyeWalkers" /> Dooku went on to claim that Viceroy Gunray had served Sidious at Naboo, but had been betrayed and abandoned by the Sith when he no longer served a useful purpose. During the ensuing [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|battle]] and the showdown between Dooku and Grand Master Yoda, Dooku's actions revealed that he was indeed in league with the Sith but not whether he was the master or the apprentice.<ref name="Episode 2">{{Film|II}}</ref> Rumor spread quickly at the Jedi Temple of the possibility of a second Sith being involved in Republic [[Politics/Legends|politics]]. Most Jedi continued to dismiss this as too far-fetched to even consider: the Jedi would be aware of a Sith takeover within the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. Many Jedi, including Kenobi, believed that Dooku was using this as a deception to cover up his own fall to the dark side and to paint himself in a stronger light.

Despite this, several marginalized Jedi dissented from the status quo. Jedi Master [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] went undercover on behalf of Master [[Tholme/Legends|Tholme]] in hopes of corroborating the existence of the second Sith. Vos went so far undercover that hunting the elusive Sith became his obsession and his only claim to his former identity. Dooku understood this and sent Vos on a [[List of phrases and slang#W|wild bantha chase]] across Coruscant, convincing Vos that Senator [[Viento]] was actually a Sith Lord. Infiltrating Viento's apartment, Vos did battle with his fellow Jedi Master [[K'Kruhk]] and nearly killed him, as he assassinated the Senator. Realizing he had been deceived, Vos eventually returned to the Order proper, but still harbored his belief that Dooku was simply the apprentice. Jedi [[Gokim Keeg]] was another dissenting member of the Order, believing that Dooku's claims were not a ruse and actually held some truth.

During the early phases of the Clone Wars, Jedi Master Mace Windu and Jedi Padawan [[Halagad Ventor]] suspected the [[mutant]] [[Geneticist/Legends|genetic]] [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorist]] [[Zeta Magnus]] as being the second Sith or closely associated with them. Zeta Magnus was an escaped [[Arkanian/Legends|Arkanian]] [[Accelerated Transgenic Heuristic Abhorer|experiment]] who committed many atrocities and [[Bioengineering/Legends|bioengineered]] numerous weapons for the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]]. Zeta Magnus's primary moniker included the ancient Sith title[[Magnus (Sith)|"Magnus]]" meaning "All-Powerful", "Lord of Lords", or "Emperor". His alias "Saturna the Garu" was a reference to the Sith Lord [[Garu]] from the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]]. The mutant also wore [[Armor/Legends|armor]] inspired by the ancient [[Magus Sentinel|Magi Sentinels]] of [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon's]] [[Iziz ruling family|dark-side theocracy]]. Zeta Magnus purposefully made himself appear to be the second Sith to throw the Jedi off Sidious's trail and to subtly mock his Sith master.<ref name="SkyeWalkers" />

===Resolution===
By the height of the Clone Wars, most of the Jedi High Council feared that the Sith had penetrated the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military's]] highest echelons as several coincidences and discrepancies were made apparent. Mace Windu in particular became concerned with those surrounding the [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]], believing that he was but a puppet of the Sith. Windu's suspicion fell on Senate [[Vice Chair/Legends|Vice Chair]] [[Mas Amedda/Legends|Mas Amedda]], Palpatine's personal advisor [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]], and his mysterious [[Red Guard]]s.<ref name="LoE">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref>

However, the reappearance of Darth Maul temporarily led the Jedi astray from the true identity of the second Sith. At the height of the conflict between Maul's [[Shadow Collective/Legends|Shadow Collective]] and Sidious' power base, the temporarily alliance forged between Maul and Dooku caused Windu to believe that Maul was the Sith apprentice and Dooku was the Sith Master.<ref name="Son of Dathomir 3">[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 3|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 3]]</ref> In a similar vein, during the [[Siege of Saleucami]], Quinlan Vos strongly suspected that the second Sith was [[Sora Bulq/Legends|Sora Bulq]]. Bulq, however, was killed in a confrontation with the Jedi Master.

Only when Master Kenobi recovered the [[Mechno-chair/Legends|mechno-chair]] of Viceroy Gunray could the High Council definitively link Dooku with some mysterious, shadowy figure. Two members of the council were convinced that Dooku was the master, having been self-taught by a [[Sith holocron/Legends|Sith holocron]] he uncovered or ancient lore found on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. As more evidence presented itself in the final weeks of the war, Yoda revealed the hunt for the second Sith to Supreme Chancellor Palpatine and informed him of an ongoing investigation in [[The Works/Legends|the Works]] district of Coruscant. The Jedi had tracked the Sith to an abandoned building there and believed that the Sith was using it as a base.
